- When sentiment is consistently neutral or low (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows increasing bullishness (e.g., >0.50), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day average is >72, forecast should not exceed 74 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is high (1.00 or above), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 2–4% if sentiment >0.75.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if true outcome shows 2+ consecutive drops, forecast should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% per drop.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70.5, model often overcorrects upward; cap forecast at 71.5 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
